subject: cholesky factor for correlation matrices + more on testing, merging, etc.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: cholesky factor for correlation matrices + more on testing, merging, etc.
parts:
I pushed a branch from develop that has everything stubbed
out that we'll need to add a Cholesky factor of correlation matrices
type:

feature/corr-cholesky-type

Sorry there's not an issue, but I started doing this on the
plane w/o an internet connection. Is there a way to change
the name of a branch?

What we need to add is:

- change underlying unconstrained params to (N choose 2)
- write the transforms in prob/transform.hpp

Ben --- if you have some time in Dec, we should get
together and plug in the right transforms. If you can
lend a hand (perhaps both sitting down together), it should
go very quickly.

Does this also need to allow rectangular sizes? And are
there constraints on the rectangular sizes for the ordinary
Cholesky factors for symmetric, positive definite matrices?

Then I can take it from there and hopefully get some
help from Daniel on testing. As is, there are ZERO unit
tests for the parser and generator. Only some whole model
parsability and compilability tests, and of course some model
tests using the constructs. So we need to get our
testing maven, Daniel, involved, too.

We are going to talk about the whole testing and
merging process at the meeting tomorrow. Having talked
to Daniel informally, I believe his major concern is that
new functionality gets tested at least a little bit and that
we continue to retrofit tests for existing functionality.

I think this emphasis on testing is a very good idea,
but we need to work out some priorities and guidelines
so we're not all guessing at what needs to be done. For
the parser and generator, we'll probably need to break apart
some of the code to do more modular testing.

- Bob
